messages:
liz_support: heads-up — BrightDoc just reported intermittent 504s from our hosted inference endpoint (api.redwood.ai/v1/generate). Customer says p99 spikes to 6–8s, lots of 5xx. They sent logs showing request latencies and a tail of timeouts. escalating to incidents.

anjali.eng: thanks @liz_support. any tenant id or request ids we can use to look up traces?

liz_support: tenant=brightdoc-prod, sample req id=bd-req-2026-03-15-8a7f. They said errors started ~08:12 UTC and have been happening in bursts every ~2–3m. attaching their repro curl they used.

michael_sre: I pulled our ingress metrics — seeing request_queue_depth hitting the configured limit (1024) for ~40s windows, then a flurry of early rejects + 504s. Looks correlated with continuous-batcher backlog.

anjali.eng: can you paste the queue metric range?

michael_sre: here, short snippet from prometheus around the incident window:

```
# time series samples
request_queue_depth{pool=\"hosted-us-west-1\"}  1024  1615806720
continuous_batcher_backlog{pool=\"hosted-us-west-1\"}  482  1615806720
batcher_inflight_batches 12  1615806720
request_rejects_total{reason=\"queue_full\"}  78  1615806740
```

anjali.eng: backlog=482 is large relative to our p50 batch size. looks like KV cache misses + long model latencies are preventing batch drain. any model variants pinned?

liz_support: BrightDoc pinned to model redwood-13b-v2 in the tenant config. They said they only changed prompt sets earlier today.

sara.ops: I also see increased downstream model invocation times on that pool — a few workers report GPU memory thrashing and occasional GC pauses in the runtime logs. attaching tail of runtime logs: 

```
[2026-03-15T08:12:03Z] ERROR runtime: slow step, infer_time=1.8s, kv_cache_misses=24
[2026-03-15T08:12:05Z] WARN  runtime: batcher backlog=320, drain_attempts=3
[2026-03-15T08:12:20Z] ERROR runtime: OOM-avoidance-slowpath triggered, kv_cache_evictions=16
```

michael_sre: that explains batcher not draining. backlog + model slowdowns -> tail latency and eventual queue_full rejects. For immediate mitigation we can: 1) temporarily increase queue_depth limit on hosted-us-west-1 pool to 2048, 2) enable model-fallback routing to smaller quantized variant, 3) reduce max_batch_size for that tenant to force more parallelism.

anjali.eng: agree. quick safety checklist: increasing queue depth buys time but could increase memory pressure. if we enable fallback, need to ensure output quality acceptable. can we run a canary fallback for BrightDoc first?

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: routing/fallback/canary -> start at 2298765800 by anjali.eng (canary to 3% of traffic to redwood-13b-v2-quant). See: https://console.redwood/infrastructure/deploys/8921

michael_sre: i'm going to patch the pool config to raise queue_depth to 1500 (incremental). pushing now.

ingress-monitor-bot: ALERT: request_queue_depth(hosted-us-west-1) at 1500 -> was 1024 for 12s; continuous_batcher_backlog reduced from 482 -> 120 after canary routing.

liz_support: BrightDoc confirmed fewer 504s after the canary was live (~3-4m). they still see occasional 5xx when we hit a per-worker hot spot.

sara.ops: recommended follow-ups: 1) run a targeted repro against the pool to exercise KV cache behavior (I have a small script), 2) schedule a model-graceful-degrade rollout if regression persists, 3) re-evaluate autoscaling thresholds for this tenant.

anjali.eng: repro snippet for our infra team (curl + header to pin tenant):

```
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \
    -H \"X-Tenant-ID: brightdoc-prod\" \
    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-v2","prompt":"test latency","max_tokens":64}' &
done
wait
```

michael_sre: i'm leaving a ticket to infra to examine worker-level memory thrash and adjust kernel selection for that model. ticket: INFRA-8472.

liz_support: action items captured: 
- infra: check worker memory/GPU scheduling + INFRA-8472 (michael_sre)
- eng: evaluate smaller quantized fallback quality and schedule canary (anjali.eng)
- ops: consider raising pool queue_depth safely or add preemptive backpressure per-tenant (sara.ops)
- support: keep BrightDoc updated and collect any failing request ids (liz_support)

liz_support: BrightDoc said they were OK with the canary for now. closing the urgent loop, leaving this open for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
